bugs.creator: michaelchirico4
bugs.summary: checkPoFile() should endeavor to point out non-ASCII format entries

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
Consider:

```
# \UFF53: ｓ = "FULLWIDTH LATIN SMALL LETTER S"
cat('msgid "%s"\nmsgstr "%\UFF53"\n', file=po <- tempfile(fileext=".po"))
tools::checkPoFile(po)
# /tmp/RtmpnmXGUH/file1c15537729694.po:2
# unrecognised format specification '%ｓ'
# %s
# %ｓ
```

We can imagine seeing this error with hazy eyes and not quite knowing what's wrong. I'm sure there are better UTF-8-vs-ASCII twin examples out there too. Moreover this type of mistake is common as translators may forget to switch keyboards as they are writing messages.

So I think we should try and do better to point out "Maybe you meant '%s'?".

I know that we can use `iconv("%ｓ", to="ASCII//TRANSLIT")` to find the ASCII `s` that was intended, but I'm not sure how robust this is across platforms, and also not sure they best way to incorporate that to the existing code -- the current error is coming from the C routine `getfmts`:

https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/blob/f12b29bb485bc6ca4e0dce83ce7b03d9987de760/src/library/tools/src/getfmts.c#L96

Filing the issue first to probe interest before getting too involved in a patch.
